newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Six-day strike ends at Moscow's Bykovo airport.
newsitem.headline: Six-day strike ends at Moscow's Bykovo airport.

text.p: Air traffic controllers have ended a six-day strike that paralysed Moscow's Bykovo domestic airport, a strike committee official said on Tuesday.
"We began to service regular and charter flights from Monday night after an agreement with the Federal Aviation Service (FAS) was signed," he told Reuters by telephone.
Controllers began the strike last Wednesday, demanding higher salaries and benefits.
The official said the FAS met most of the strikers' demands but gave no further details.

Bykovo airport served 11 departures and 15 arrivals on Tuesday, the official said. Usually, the airport operates about 40 regular and domestic flights daily to 25 destinations in central Russia, the Urals and Siberia.
In August, Russian aviation union leaders called for a general strike, but 60,000 pilots, traffic controllers and ground service specialists did not support them.
Air traffic controllers struck for higher pay in 1992 and their disruption of domestic flights led to three cases of aircraft coming dangerously close to one another in the air.
